sonnet.problem: The question's setup, 'The king's command is urgent and the furnace is blazing,' carries the cause given in verse 22 and rules out the wrong answers. Because the command is urgent, 'They refuse the order' is eliminated, and 'blazing' points straight to 'The flames kill them.'
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: Card 10's right answer already says the four men are 'walking around unharmed.' Card 11 then asks whether they are still tied up, which is the same verse 25 fact ('unbound and unharmed') and is answered by card 10.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.
